ObjectName.value: C-band Radar-dish Antenna

Categories.value: Radar antennas|Parabolic antennas|PD NASA|Structures at Kennedy Space Center|Images from NASA with broken source

ImageDescription.value:
KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLA. – This new C-band, 3 megawatt radar with a 50-foot dish antenna has recently been installed on north Kennedy Space Center. It is one of the largest of its kind in the world, providing higher definition imagery than has ever been available before. Working in concert with two new NASA-owned X-band radars mounted on the solid rocket booster retrieval ships, tracking the space shuttle and expendable launch vehicles with this new capability will provide more detail than NASA has ever observed by radar before. The first use of this C-band radar will be for the launch of the Atlas V rocket sending the New Horizons probe toward Pluto. The radar is operated under a NASA contract with the U.S. Navy who owns the radar.
ITU-classificatio: C band Radiolocation land station in the radiolocation service.

ImageDescription.value: The image shows a radar station forming part of the Spanish SIVE surveillance system (Sistema Integrado de Vigilancia Exterior) at the foot of Na Penyal mountain in eastern Mallorca, Balearic Islands. The installation is located within the municipality of Sant Llorenç des Cardassar, close to the towns of Son Servera and Cala Millor. The radar station consists of a steel lattice tower equipped with parabolic, microwave and other radio antennas, mounted on a solid concrete base. It forms part of the technical infrastructure used for coastal and external surveillance, surrounded by Mediterranean scrub vegetation.

152691336.title: File:Surveillance radar antenna DR-1 of BMEWS site at Clear Air Force Station, Alaska (photo HAER AK-30-A-11).jpg

ObjectName.value: Surveillance radar antenna DR-1 of BMEWS site at Clear Air Force Station, Alaska (photo HAER AK-30-A-11)

Categories.value: Clear Space Force Station|Parabolic torus reflector antennas|PD US NPS|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation

ImageDescription.value:
DR-1, one of 3 antennas of the AN/FPS-50 surveillance radar of the US Air Force Ballistic Missile Early Warning System (BMEWS) site II at Clear, Alaska. Built in 1961 in the Cold War and closed in 2001, BMEWS was an arctic-based system of radars and computers to detect a nuclear ICBM attack on the US from Russia over the North Pole. It's extreme northern location was designed to give an early enough warning (15 - 30 minutes) that US missiles could be launched and bombers could take off, reducing the chance of a preemptive nuclear strike on the US.

The original photo's description was:

View of south side of radar scanner building no. 104 showing personnel exit door at side building, showing DR 1 antenna from oblique angle on foundation berm with DR 2 and DR 3 antennae in background. - Clear Air Force Station, Ballistic Missile Early Warning System Site II, One mile west of mile marker 293.5 on Parks Highway, 5 miles southwest of Anderson, Anderson, Denali Borough, AK
